In today’s episode, we sit down with Bryson DeChambeau, Professional Golfer, to understand how he approaches golf differently and what it takes to perform at the highest level.

We discuss how he transformed his body to hit the ball farther, the science behind speed training, and how technology helped change his game. Bryson explains how he measures performance, builds a repeatable golf swing, and uses experimentation to find an edge over his competitors.

The conversation also covers the mental pressure of professional golf, the risks of overtraining, recovering from injuries, and why sleep is critical for performance. He also shares how he balances professional golf with building his YouTube channel and creating content around his passion for the game.

👉 Video Introduction

Why do some consumer brands become household names while thousands of others disappear, even with great products and millions in funding?

And how does an investor spot the next Sula, Epigamia or Bombay Sweet Shop before the rest of the market catches on?

Deepak Shahdadpuri, Founder of DSG Consumer Partners, has backed over 100 consumer brands and witnessed India's consumer revolution from the front row. From investing in Sula before India's wine industry existed to backing brands like Epigamia, Go Zero and Bombay Sweet Shop, he has developed a playbook for identifying, building and scaling India's next generation of consumer businesses.

In this episode, he breaks down what makes a brand truly irreplaceable, why founders should focus on their first 1,000 customers instead of trying to capture all of India, and why a business can die with the gross margins it is born with.

In this episode, you'll learn:
- The 4-stage framework every successful consumer brand must cross: Awareness, Trial, Repeat and Scale.
- The secret behind building a brand that customers refuse to replace, even when competitors offer alternatives.
- Why India's next big consumer brands may come from categories that already exist in the West but are still unexplored in India.
- Why you don't need 1.4 billion customers to build a ₹100 crore business.
- The 3 financial benchmarks DSG uses to identify genuinely successful and capital-efficient consumer businesses.
- Why founders who solve problems they personally experience often outperform those chasing large market opportunities.
- The biggest red flags Deepak looks for before investing in a founder, including the personality traits that can make or break a business.
- Why AI search could completely change how consumers discover brands, and why Reddit communities may become critical for brand visibility.

videos.title: Do the Thing You Least Want to Do (It Grows This Part of Your Brain) | Dr. Andrew Huberman
videos.description:
Your brain doesn't want easy. It wants predictable. That's why some hard things can make you feel safe.

In this clip, Andrew Huberman and Jay Shetty talk about why our friendships feel weaker as our followers keep growing. Huberman says every brain needs two things before it can feel close to anyone. And he explains why the things that are good for us feel so hard at first.

Huberman says a cold plunge isn't about pushing yourself. He shares a question to ask before you get in, and why you should count walls, not minutes. Jay shares a tense talk he had the day before, and the phrase that calmed it down. 

Learn about a part of the brain most people have never heard of. And learn why the thing you least want to do might be the thing that makes it grow.

JAY'S DAILY WISDOM DELIVERED STRAIGHT TO YOUR INBOX
